full: There is no stable llama.cpp. There never was. You are waiting anyway; the maintainer: not at the moment. You downloaded a build weeks ago and cannot say which number. Nothing pings you; your copy drifts. Today stamped six releases; three inside one hour, eleven eleven to eleven fifty-eight. Each build is one named change: a Vulkan fix, a WebGPU kernel, a server scheduling fix. Each ships forty prebuilt downloads. Never measured? Then pinning costs nothing you can see. No upstream speed number exists, so yours comes from llama-bench, the tool that counts your tokens per second. Tonight: check, re-pin, re-run llama-bench. Old row, new row: the update is a number, not a vibe.
